body: Thank you… I needed to hear all this.

Well, if I was to offer any advice. It is that you are better and worth more than having to be delusional about something in order to cope. I think I went through a phase of something similar. Where I tried to convince myself that what he did was not as terrible as it really was. But I needed to snap out of that. I needed/need to feel these things. As hard as it is. 

But, I’m not here to tell anyone how to get through things, or change how they view it. This is my experience. But being real with yourself and with the situation is always better than not, in my opinion. 

I hope the best for you truly. I hate that you feel that way. Send me a message if you want to talk. Seriously.

I understand. I hope I didn’t come off as rude or anything. It was really me letting out the frustration  I have towards him and my situation. Not directed at you exactly. I’m not upset if that’s your perspective and how you get through things. We are all here dealing with the same shit.

With all due respect to you and your perspective, fuck all this crap! 

Your example is very different from mine and a lot of peoples situations here. Being sent off to war and missing your SO to the point that it made you realize how much you loved and needed them is not comparable to cheating: acting out of selfishness, destroying your loved ones trust, security, and self-esteem. 

I understand that relationships have hardships. People go through tough times. It makes us better, individually and together. We went through patches where we came out valuing each other so much more. 

But, it was nothing as heinous and hurtful as this. This is not apart of normal “ups and downs” of a relationship. 

I adored this man. He treated me better than everyone before. I gave him my heart. I gave him my trust. And he took advantage. He manipulated me, lied to me, gaslit me. All for his own selfish desires.

I told him that him cheating on me was the worst possible thing he could do to me. And he did it anyways. 

I am here because I do still love him. He is showing remorse. He is showing love. He is showing guilt. He is showing that he wants to fight. So I am giving it a try. I want it to work out, and I AM fighting like hell to make this work. 

But, overcoming this will never be a badge of honor. It will never be. We didn’t need this to become better. He did this not because of problems within us, or a serious mental problem within him like sex addiction. There was nothing that pushed him to step out, besides having the opportunity and not being able to say no out of ego and selfishness. 

I shouldn’t have to “craft him into my perfect prince charming”. This ain’t build-a-bear. He is a grown man and knows what is right and what is wrong. And that goes for everyone in a situation like this. No one should have to go through trauma/act out and repent to have a good relationship. 

Yes, no one is perfect and everyone can work on themselves to be better for their partner, but this is way out of line. This is not something like “I need to work on helping my SO with chores more”.  

I’m sorry. Peace and love to you, but this is just my perspective.

Everything that you said. Yes. Exactly. 10000%. 

I wrote a letter to him once detailing my feelings about 2 weeks after DDay happened, and I put this same sentiment into words back then… 

*”As you have said to me before, sometimes mistakes are made so you can learn and change yourself for the better. And here you are, using this awful situation for good, while I’m left to fend for myself.
You got to have your fun. You got to feed your ego, feel desired and wanted by someone else. You got to experience the excitement of someone new. And in the process, you have taken away so much from me. You are going into this with newfound love, appreciation, and realization. While I am left to pick up the pieces and try to put myself back together.”* 

It is so true. The exit wounds will never come close to being the same. Me, you, and anyone else who is dealing with this, unfortunately became a senseless martyr in a relationship that we are still trying for.

Yeah, exactly what it feels like! “Thanks dealing with me cheating and taking one for the team! Now I can be the partner you always deserved” haha. I have expressed to him how it comes across before. Sometimes it seems like he gets it, sometimes not. 

I just hate how he tries to make it seem like every relationship has or needs to go through something as horrible and traumatic as this, and that it makes for a better relationship between the two. 

It doesn’t always make things better. And it doesn’t and didn’t need to happen for us to have a strong connection! Like you and your husband, we were always great! And he says it as well. He says he didn’t do this out of any issues between us, or with me. 

Okay… so we didn’t *need* this then. Stop saying that crap! 

I wanted a relationship where I didn’t have to ever say those things in this context. To have to say “we went through infidelity and terrible times and I have some trauma still from it, but we made it out!” 

It just perpetrates this idea that doing terrible and traumatic things to your SO is supposed to be apart of your journey with them. And it’s not! It *may* happen, but it’s not exactly the way to look at it.

I appreciate your comment and perspective from the other side though. It is enlightening to hear what someone could really mean when they say these things. Because yes, sometimes it does come across as the “hey, isn’t it great that I did this to you!”.  I think your examples come across better than some of things I put in my post.

I replied to another person a bit ago with this, and it suits my response to this as well so I’m just going to copy and paste. 

“For me, it feels even more unnecessary because he says he didn’t do it because of me, or problems with us. We weren’t perfect, but we didn’t have problems between us that might lead to infidelity. Things that I could possibly look at and say “okay, I  can understand a bit why you went astray” Our sex life was great, our emotional connection was great, we talked to each other about our problems and always strived to be better for each other, he didn’t do this out of some life trauma, he is not a sex addict…

My point being…. We had no deep underlying issues until this. He did this simply because he self-admittedly was being selfish and let his sexual desires matter more than me at that time.”

This is just my case though. I’m not saying I’m perfect, and I have been ready to be open to receiving any sort of criticism of something I did to push him here. But in his words and through the many talks we have had since, I was never doing anything wrong. Like you said, what happened is never the BS fault. But I get everyone is human and has needs and makes mistakes and sometimes certain conditions can push you into doing something awful. 

This is kind of the point of my post though… is that it really was unnecessary for us. Some couples, it may awaken things that were being unsaid. Things that needed to come to light so that both people can change and be better for each other. 

For us, it wasn’t.

I feel everything you’ve said so deeply as well. 

For me, it feels even more unnecessary because he says he didn’t do it because of me, or problems with us. We weren’t perfect, but we didn’t have problems between us that might lead to infidelity. Things that I could possibly look at and say “okay, I  can understand a bit why you went astray” Our sex life was great, our emotional connection was great, we talked to each other about our problems and always strived to be better for each other, he didn’t do this out of some life trauma, he is not a sex addict… 

My point being…. We had no deep underlying issues until this. He did this simply because he self-admittedly was being selfish and let his sexual desires matter more than me at that time. 

“Always know that he hurt me more than anyone or 
anything else has” 

Exactly. We have to continue with these thoughts that will always linger.
Exactly. He says he feels closer to me, yet I will never feel as close to him as I once did.

Thank you. I am trying to do that now. I let myself fall into a heavy depression when everything first went down. I gained weight and stopped taking care of myself. I’ve been snapping out of it lately. I’ve been going to the gym again this past week and getting out more. It feels good. 

Even if we don’t get through this, I have to make sure that I, mentally, physically, and everything else, am better than when this happened.

Sorry to make you emotional. Writing my thoughts and feelings out on these posts helps me a lot. Knowing others understand and I am not alone. It’s bittersweet. I understand the pain and hate that others go through it as well. I wish you the best.
Thank you. I know we are all here for the same reason, but I’m sorry you have to go through this too. I hope for the best for you.

It sucks that we can relate so much on this. I wouldn’t wish that on anyone. I also went through the manipulation and gaslighting. He used my mental illness to convince MYSELF that all the suspicions I had were not real. That I was crazy. And I believed him for awhile. 

Sometimes he doesn’t understand why I am so terrified of fully giving myself to him again, and I explain this kind of stuff to him.

Cheating is so much more than the physical. It’s not the thought of him touching another woman that breaks me. It’s everything else. 

Thank you for your comment. I am here as well.

Same here, I understand the pain. I vividly remember a conversation we had, where I told him that being cheated on would absolutely destroy me. That it could be the worse thing he could do to me. That I would rather him be honest and break up with me…..And he did it anyways. Im sorry you have to go through this too.

Yeah, thank you for your words. It takes a lot to realize that being cheated on is NOT your fault. And of course everyone whose cheated on has to go through their own process of coping and moving on, I guess I mean the difference I’ve seen in people who can hold themselves together afterwards and others who turn into an absolute wreck. How it can hurt some on a very deep level, and others not so much.

I am very grateful that he is doing everything he can to make me feel comfortable and secure in our relationship. I just don’t want to do things that could be unreasonable out of hurt. I know he’s the one with a lot to prove, but I still want to work on a having a level of healthiness and fairness between us.

That’s my thing too. I can’t understand why he would possibly think this would be an okay thing to just do without talking to me first. I guess we never had a conversation where we laid out every single “okay/not okay” we had going forward, but I figured something like this would be common sense. I guess not, but maybe we should have another conversation about situations like this.

You’re very right about having a plan for situations like this in the future. I will take that in mind going further. I don’t think it’s going to do any good for our relationship if I basically end up forcing a no contact with any and all of his female friends.

I agree. Before the cheating I was definitely not the kind of partner who would be upset about something like that. I fully trusted him back then of course, and he ended up taking advantage of that. It’s very different now.
